story_text.value:
Hey HN, I wanted to show you something I built. I actually built it last year but the prices of VPS instances went to the moon and I shelved it until recently. It's called Whitehirst (I had the .com domain lying around, hence the name!)

You can spin up a Sovereign UK/EU Windows Workstation in ~10 minutes that's fully configured with all the dev tools you'll need like Visual Studio 2026, VS Code, Docker CE, Git, Rust, NVM, Tailscale and more. It's a custom Windows Server 2022 rig that removes all the bloat, telemetry and Copilot stuff. I've spent an obscene length of time perfecting the build so it runs incredibly fast.

You can spin up a rig for 8 or 24 hours with zero risk of a surprise cloud bill as every workstation is strictly ephemeral and automatically self-destructs when time's up (prices are £12 for 8 hours or £25 for 24 hours). You can extend your time if you wish. I'm only offering a single spec at the moment: 8 AMD EPYC vCPUs, 32GB ECC RAM, 200GB NVMe storage and a 2Gbps nic - I intend to offer other specs later on.

If you'd like to try it, head to https://whitehirst.com and fill out the contact form and I'll pick a handful to get started with. I'm going to keep the numbers small for now so that I can make sure it all works and I can iron out the bugs since it's still in early-access.

Anyway, let me know what you think.

Ta

Mick

https://whitehirst.com

story_text.value:
Hi, I built an hancrafted HTML-first JavaScript framework called Places.js that outperforms React, Svelte, Lit, and Vue.

- Components are created with HTML-first templating, which allows for flexibility in how HTML is generated.

- No build step. Places.js can be downloaded from a CDN and directly added to a project.

- JavaScript enhanced web components that can be dynamically rendered with API endpoint data.

- Rendering agnostic stores that can be integrated with other frameworks.

To test Places.js,download the latest version from JSDelivr:https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/createthirdplaces/places-js@0.1....

Here is a reference guide: https://createthirdplaces.org/tech/placesjs/reference/presen...

Other links:

Benchmarks for Places.js and other frameworks:https://krausest.github.io/js-framework-benchmark/2026/chrom...

Event listing site I made with Places.js: https://dmvboardgames.com/

title.value: Show HN: Handcrafted HTML-first framework that outperforms React

story_text.value:
Hello, my name is Berend Graham. My cofounder Shiv Oberai and I have been working on Limma for a year now with the goal of building a proactive solution to the reliability issues that plague practical AI and agentic use in companies with RAG.

Limma is a single MCP that exists for the sole purpose of ensuring that the right information is retrieved with every query and no information is skipped and or missed. This means total precision and recall. We've found that this approach leads to the lowest rate of hallucination vs. solely targeting agent action verification which has made tremendous strides in capability.

We do this by building a map and structuring all data-points within unstructured data as well as federating structured data for addressability so that agents don't need to search through chunks directly and instead only get the right information . We wanted this to be extremely easy to use so that anyone can set it up and try it within minutes so that the precision issues (especially with large quantities of data) that LLMs struggle with can finally be remedied. We use self-hosted models (primarily Qwen models as of current) so that the system can be deployed on one's own server if needed, and also to optimize for speed.

We have a free monthly version on our website if anyone would like to try it out and provide feedback!

title.value: Show HN: Limma – MCP for total recall and precision in data retrieval for agents
